dossier.public_summary: The dip alternates shallow and deep every orbit with a deep second eclipse half an orbit between the two, both much too deep for a planet around this star. The depth also changes dramatically between sectors, from undetectable to very deep. Together this shows the 11-day signal is from a grazing eclipsing binary on the target, not a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even dips differ strongly, as expected for a binary seen at half the 11 d period (22 d). This is positive evidence for an eclipsing binary on the target, not a planet.

A second deep dip ~58% as deep as the primary, inconsistent with a planetary secondary (V-shaped and large despite flat primary shape v_sigma -16.17). Indicates stellar eclipses at 0.784 phase and opposite phase, not an occultation.
reasons.value: 27.95 at phase 0.784 depth 60.9 ppm depth_over_dip 0.5856 best_brightening_snr 13.8

reasons.why: Depth is not steady; SPOC 2-min shows large genuine changes (verdict changes_within_a_source) and sector 36 depth 825 ppm vs ~100 ppm elsewhere. Real planet should be steady; this variability plus a high-ranking binary signature points to systematics/combined eclipses on the target.
Large out-of-eclipse modulation comparable to the dip depth supports a close stellar companion/spots-driven EB, not a planet.
No off-target neighbour can explain it; the signal is on/in the target, so the odd/even and secondary are from an EB on the target, not a blend.
